text: Given a stub platform answering {success:true,data:{id:'a1',prompt:'<long>',updatedAt:'T'}}, When upsert_agent_approval is called with valid rules, Then the result is exactly {success:true,id:'a1',updatedAt:'T'} and the prompt text is absent
Given the same stub, When upsert_agent_permissions is called with a valid permission map, Then the result is exactly {success:true,id:'a1',updatedAt:'T'} with no permissionEffective and no prompt
Given the same stub, When upsert_agent_evaluation is called with a rule that has a rubric, Then the result is exactly {success:true,id:'a1',updatedAt:'T'}
Given a stub that records the PUT body, When each of the three tools saves, Then the body sent is unchanged from before (only the response is trimmed)

Given the stub raises AgentError(400,'boom') or answers {success:false,error:'Agent not found'} or rules lack a rubric, When each tool is called, Then the error text equals the one returned before this change (success:false bodies pass through unchanged)
Given a stub answer with a 20 KB prompt, When each of the three tools succeeds, Then the response is under 1024 bytes
On INT with a test agent in the test tenant: call each save tool then the matching get tool; the get returns the values just saved
precond: A test agent exists in the test tenant on INT
steps: 1) Call mspbotsagent_upsert_agent_approval with one rule. 2) Call mspbotsagent_get_agent_approval. 3) Repeat with upsert_agent_permissions/get_agent_permissions and upsert_agent_evaluation/get_agent_evaluation.
expect: Each get returns the values just saved.

text: On INT with the same test agent: each of the three save calls returns only success, id and updatedAt, and the raw response is under 1 KB
steps: 1) Call each of the three save tools with a valid payload. 2) Record each raw response and its byte length.
expect: Each response contains only success, id and updatedAt and is under 1 KB.

text: On INT: call upsert_agent_evaluation with a rule without rubric and upsert_agent_permissions with an unknown bare tool id; both return their previous error text
steps: 1) Call upsert_agent_evaluation with a rule that has no rubric. 2) Call upsert_agent_permissions with permission {"send_email":"allow"}.
expect: Both return the same invalid_argument error text as before this change.
